info.name: OAN A2C — Farmer B2C Flow
info.description:
End-to-end farmer self-service flow: register with a phone number, log in, browse the catalog, bookmark, build a Draft application, submit it to a bank, and read it back.

Run the folders in order. Folder 2 is a hard prerequisite on a fresh account — a farmer with no bound A2C Farmer Profile cannot create anything.

Actors are kept in separate variables (farmer_jwt, dev_agent_jwt) rather than a shared jwt_token, so this collection can be merged into the combined one without clobbering its token mid-run.

Endpoints covered: api.v1.auth.register_user, api.auth.login, api.auth.get_me, api.v1.farmer.catalog.*, api.v1.farmer.applications.*, api.v1.farmer.dashboard.*

item.name: 1. Farmer Account
item.description:
DEVELOPMENT LOGIN ONLY. In production a farmer authenticates over OAuth against the Fayda farmer registry; email + password is the stand-in until that lands, so treat this folder as scaffolding rather than the real entry path.

Registration mints a fresh farmer each run, so the folder is safe to re-run. The phone number is still collected — the consent webhook matches a User to a farmer profile by mobile_no — but it is not an identity and nothing logs in with it.

request.description:
email is required for every role, farmers included — there is no identifier to derive one from, and a missing address is a field-level 400 from RegisterUserSchema. phone_number is still required and still stored on the User, because the consent webhook binds a farmer profile by mobile_no.

Rate limited two ways: 50/60s per IP and 5/60s per phone number, so shared carrier NAT does not lock out a village.

item.name: 3. Farmer Profile Binding (verify)
item.description:
STOP HERE ON A FRESH ACCOUNT. Every write endpoint in folders 3 and 4 resolves the caller through A2C Farmer Profile where user = session user, and a freshly registered farmer has no such profile — create_application and save_product both throw "You must have a Farmer Profile".

Binding is done by the consent-data webhook (api/v1/webhook_consent_data.py:315-331): it matches a User by mobile_no/phone, checks the A2C Farmer role, and sets profile.user. That path needs a lead, an OpenG2P consent and an api_key/api_secret pair, so it lives in the combined collection under "4. OpenG2P Consent Flow" + "Loan Application Management".

For local testing the deterministic shortcut is bench console:

  bench --site development.localhost console
  >>> import frappe
  >>> phone = "<farmer_phone from the run log>"
  >>> user = frappe.db.get_value("User", {"mobile_no": phone}, "name")
  >>> p = frappe.get_doc({"doctype": "A2C Farmer Profile", "first_name": "Test",
  ...     "last_name": "Farmer", "phone_number": phone, "user": user})
  >>> p.insert(ignore_permissions=True); frappe.db.commit()

Run "1. Verify Profile Bound" afterwards to confirm before continuing.

item.name: 5. Application Lifecycle
item.description:
Draft is the farmer's working stage: they create, edit and then submit it. Submission moves the application to Processing through the workflow, which is the point it becomes visible to the bank (bank users never see Draft — loan_application_scope_query).

Run this folder in order; each request feeds the next through application_id.
